identity.name: Speedmaster Professional
identity.one_liner: The 1969-1973 Speedmaster Professional with the caliber 861 — the reference worn on Apollo 11 and the first Moon landing.

narrative.story: The 145.022-69 is the Speedmaster Professional that Buzz Aldrin wore on the Moon on July 20, 1969 (Neil Armstrong's Speedmaster was left on the Lunar Module; the 145.012 Aldrin left on the lunar surface is now at the Smithsonian). The caliber 861 is the cam-driven chronograph that replaced the 321 in 1968; it has a 45-minute counter and a 12-hour totalizer but is otherwise simpler. The 145.022-69 is the most-cited Moon watch and the most-cited Speedmaster in the secondary market, with the "Pre-Moon" nickname identifying any 105.003, 105.012, or 145.012 produced before the 1969 lunar landing.
narrative.collector_notes: The 145.022-69 has the "STEP" dial (the T in SPEEDMASTER is on the same line as PROFESSIONAL). The 145.022-69 is sometimes called the "Transitional" because it has the 861 caliber but the 105-series case design.
